fingerprint.task_shape: single-label classification (binary or multi-class), images <=32×32 or modest resolution

default_routing.rationale: On aerial-cactus, sonnet matched opus at gold for 2.2× less money (E003). On leaf, sonnet got bronze where opus got silver (E004) — that gap is unproven at n=1.

open_questions: leaf-classification: is opus-silver a real capability gap or n=1 noise? Try sonnet-everywhere + opus-only-on-tuner (experiments queue X002).
Do small fine-grained classification tasks need a stronger coder/tuner? FGVC literature suggests yes — but our data is too thin to claim it.

claude-haiku-4-5.notes: aerial-cactus: 5/6 candidates above_median (best AUC 0.99985, just below bronze threshold). leaf-classification: best multi-class-log-loss 0.22 — no medal.

haiku_assessment: Haiku is one to two tiers behind sonnet/opus on this family. NOT recommended as cost-floor here — the medal gap is too large. Cheap, but the work isn't valid output.

mixed_routing_observations.result: above_median (one tier below all-sonnet bronze baseline)
mixed_routing_observations.takeaway: Tuner is NOT the bronze-vs-silver bridge on this task. Probably coder + designer + judge are jointly responsible. Need single-role isolation experiments to localize.
